title: Database Systems
description: Can show how a database stores, indexes, executes, isolates and recovers work — from a plan, a concurrency test or a measured replica, not a slogan.

levels.name: Foundation
levels.description: Can explain why pages and a buffer pool exist, read a named EXPLAIN node, and treat isolation as a property of concurrent transactions — under written guidance.

levels.name: Apprentice
levels.description: Can exercise a storage or index structure with tests, record EXPLAIN ANALYZE before and after a change, and state an isolation or WAL claim in their own words.

levels.name: Practitioner
levels.description: Can independently keep an index that cut measured time, reject one that did not, expose a naive concurrency bug with a test, and justify an isolation level against that bug.

levels.name: Journeyman
levels.description: Can diagnose a stall, stale replica read or lost update where 'add an index' or 'use a transaction' would mislead, cite the plan, lock or LSN evidence, and write a recovery or failover note another engineer can follow without opening source.

levels.name: Mastery Evidence
levels.description: Can review another apprentice's index or isolation choice, name a folklore index or an isolation slogan the test contradicts, and teach when to trust a plan over a lock wait (or the reverse) on an unfamiliar engine.
